# The Redesign of Design Strategy — デザイン戦略の再定義

> A structural analysis by Satoshi Yamauchi (山内怜史), AI Strategist,
> arguing that design and business are not separate disciplines but
> different expressions of the same cognitive process: seeing through to
> the essence of a problem and structuring it (「本質を見抜き構造化する
> 眼」). The book traces how this "eye" was brought into business via
> design thinking (1999-2018), why the design firms that sold it as a
> packaged method (IDEO and 70+ others) collapsed even as design's
> business value rose, and argues that generative AI has destroyed the
> value of "execution" while leaving this "eye" as the one thing AI cannot
> replicate. As stated in the book's closing line: "本質を見抜き、構造化
> する眼。" ("The eye that sees through to the essence, and structures it.")

## Book Content

- [Full text (Japanese)](docs/jp/the_redesign_of_design_strategy_jp.md): 全6章・おわりに収録
- [Full text (English)](docs/en/the_redesign_of_design_strategy_en.md): Complete English edition

## Key Facts (as stated in the book)

- The book cites McKinsey's 2018 "The Business Value of Design" report:
  tracking 300 public companies over 5 years, design-mature companies
  outperformed industry benchmarks by 32 points in revenue growth and 56
  points in total shareholder return
- The book documents IDEO's collapse from ~725 employees and ~$300M
  revenue (2019-2020 peak) to ~$100M revenue, following layoffs in 2020
  (8%), 2023 (125 people, 25% of remaining staff), and four CEO changes
  by 2025; and cites John Maeda's Design in Tech Report finding 70+ design
  firms acquired since 2004
- The book's central explanation for this paradox: design firms sold two
  things — a personally-embodied "eye" and a commoditizable "method
  package" (workshops, research techniques). Once the method package was
  standardized by Stanford d.school and spread via books and online
  courses, companies rationally chose to hire the "eye" in-house (e.g.
  IBM grew its design team from ~230 to 3,000+, Capital One to 450+)
  rather than pay design firms for it
- The book cites Adobe Firefly generating 24B assets by May 2025 (up from
  1B in June 2023) and a UX designer job-posting decline of 71% from its
  2022 peak, alongside Nielsen Norman Group's 2025 finding that UX
  professionals are under 0.01% of the US workforce but generate 7.5% of
  all Claude conversations — the book's evidence that execution was
  automated while demand for the "eye" moved upstream rather than
  disappearing
- The book grounds its "eye" concept in prior design theory: Nigel Cross's
  "Designerly Ways of Knowing" (1982, design as a "third way of knowing"
  alongside science and the humanities), Donald Schön's "reflection-in-
  action" (1983), and Kees Dorst's "frame creation" (2015) — arguing all
  three describe the same cognitive mode the book calls "the eye"
- The book presents a 4-step method for training "the eye": (1) strip away
  the surface, (2) extract the essence, (3) visualize it as structure,
  (4) identify the leverage point — applicable across design, business,
  and engineering
- The book connects this to the author's own Depth & Velocity
  methodology: Depth is the depth of "the eye," Velocity is using AI to
  accelerate execution once the eye has defined the problem

## Author & Full Catalog

This book is one of 20+ open-source books by Satoshi Yamauchi (山内怜史),
AI Strategist & Business Designer at Sun Asterisk Inc., Founder of Leading.AI.
